desc: Prepared DT boundary from completed preflight 035: board-derived E 7-pstate and P 19-pstate OPP tables, three apple,cluster-cpufreq nodes, exact DTB a42bb096.... NOT RUNNABLE: replacement ticket 123 and then ticket 121 must first prove the first secondary and all 14 CPUs online so both P policies exist; then confirm/build CONFIG_ARM_APPLE_SOC_CPUFREQ=y, create and host-test the bounded sysfs/governor reporter, pin safe hashes, and obtain independent review. One plan-approved boot verifies E/P policy transitions. No speculative voltages or other MMIO. Rig is healthy; dependencies, not recovery, are the blocker. RESULT 2026-07-30: root cause of missing P policies was a 32-bit frequency*1000 overflow in apple-soc-cpufreq (upstream bug, first triggerable on M4 whose P clusters exceed 4.294 GHz). Fixed via patches/t6040-apple-cpufreq-freq-mult-overflow.patch; P0 verified transitioning 1.26-4.512 GHz both directions at maxcpus=5. P1 validation needs an online cluster-2 CPU (ticket 121). See evidence/2026-07-30-t6040-006-SOLVED-cpufreq-32bit-overflow.md.
author: claude
progress: 2026-07-29: reordering note. idle=nop makes idle cores SPIN (M4 loses state on WFI/WFE), so core count multiplies idle power directly - CJ observed the fan spinning up and the chassis warming at maxcpus=14. cpuidle is therefore a prerequisite for scaling SMP further and should come BEFORE cpufreq, reversing the previous plan. | 2026-07-29 CORRECTION to my own note above: calling cpuidle a PREREQUISITE for cpufreq was too strong. /proc/stat on the 5-core boot shows real idle accounting (cpu0 idle=5211 jiffies etc), so a load-based governor can see idle and downscale — cpufreq is testable and meaningful with idle=nop. cpuidle matters for POWER DRAW, not cpufreq correctness. | 2026-07-29 PATH ANALYSIS. The gate is specific: this ticket wants all three apple,cluster-cpufreq policies live, i.e. 'both P policies exist'. Cluster map is E=cpus1-4, P0=cpu0+cpus5-8, P1=cpus9-13, so a cluster-2 core needs maxcpus>=10 — blocked by the maxcpus>=6 unpack_to_rootfs fault (121). TWO WAYS FORWARD: (A) PARTIAL 006 now at maxcpus=5 — validates driver probe, the three DT nodes, the E 7-pstate and P 19-pstate OPP tables and real transitions on the E and P0 policies (2 of 3); needs CONFIG_ARM_APPLE_SOC_CPUFREQ=y (currently =m in config-macsmc-hid-type-fix-trackpad-nbcon-ppp, and the RAM image has no module loader), the cpufreq nodes merged into the wifi DTB (t6040-j614s-dcuart-wifi.dtb has ZERO cluster-cpufreq nodes; they live only in t6040-j614s-dcuart-cpufreq.dtb / a42bb096), a bounded sysfs+governor reporter, review, one attended boot. (B) FULL 006 via the 121 discriminating experiment: a DTB that disables cpu5-8 so maxcpus=6 brings up cpu0 + 4E + cpu9 — one core in EVERY cluster, hence all THREE policies at only 6 CPUs. If the fault is cluster-local (second core in the boot cluster) that config sidesteps it and unlocks full 006 with no kernel fix at all; if it still faults, the cause is a >5-CPU resource threshold and the fix is upstream-shaped. Either result is worth one boot. SAFETY: the apple cpufreq driver writes cluster p-state/APSC registers — a new MMIO class for us, though NOT PMU/charger/voltage. Normal review + attended run applies; 035 already checked APSC/pstate resources against the proven minimal path. | 2026-07-29 PARTIAL RUN DONE at maxcpus=5 (evidence/2026-07-29-t6040-006-cpufreq-partial-E-cluster-works.md). PASS on the E cluster: driver apple-cpufreq, policy1 affected_cpus=[1 2 3 4], 7 P-states 1020000..2592000 matching 035's E table EXACTLY, five governors available, and TRANSITIONS VERIFIED BOTH WAYS (performance -> 2592000, powersave -> 1020000). So the driver + DT wiring + OPP table + APSC write path all work on real hardware. OPEN: neither P cluster gets a policy; cpu0 is a P0 core and IS online yet has no cpufreq directory, and there is NO dmesg error even under greps matching this driver's own dev_err strings — so apple_soc_cpufreq_init() seems never to be CALLED for those clusters. TWO OF MY HYPOTHESES REFUTED: (1) shared opp-shared table across the two P clusters — I split it into opp-table-2 and repointed cpu_p10..p14, rebuilt DTB 43dd77ff, booted: NO CHANGE (split retained on correctness grounds only, NOT evidence-backed); (2) missing DT wiring — the DTB is correct and complete (cpu@0-3 -> 210e20000, cpu@10100-10104 -> 211e20000, cpu@10200-10204 -> 212e20000, all with operating-points-v2; the dead cpu@10105 correctly has none). Remaining correlation, NOT causation: the E cluster is the only one whose CPUs are ALL online at maxcpus=5. NEXT STEP IS CODE READING not a boot: how cpufreq_online() and of_perf_domain_get_sharing_cpumask() behave when part of the domain cpumask is offline. If that is the cause, full 006 collapses into the maxcpus>=6 SMP bug; if not, there is a second independent bug. kbuild now has a CPUFREQ=1 switch with a builtin assertion.
